metadata.title: Palo Alto Networks Stock Falls After Earnings -- Analysts See More Upside

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW) shares slid 3% Wednesday as investors reacted cautiously to the cybersecurity company's latest results despite supportive comments from Wall Street.
The company's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue reached $3.41 billion, up 34% from a year earlier, while adjusted earnings rose to $1.02 per share. Next-generation security annual recurring revenue increased 63% to $9.1 billion.
For fiscal 2027, Palo Alto expects revenue of about $14.15 billion, implying roughly 23% growth. Jefferies analyst Joseph Gallo kept a Buy rating and a $450 price target, citing room for the outlook to improve as AI-related security demand develops.
Bank of America analyst Tal Liani also maintained a Buy rating with a $420 target, saying elevated expectations may have limited the immediate stock response. J.P. Morgan's Brian Essex kept an Overweight view and a $384 target, pointing to increased cybersecurity spending as AI changes enterprise security needs.
CEO Nikesh Arora said nearly $1 trillion of existing cybersecurity infrastructure may require updates for an AI-driven environment.
Strong forecasts may support the long-term case, but elevated expectations could keep shares volatile.
